target.output: repository-host discovery dedup pin race canary evidence

problem: The discovery dedup implementation had only proved atomic create-if-absent with a local filesystem reference implementation. Repository-host behavior on the canonical GitHub proposal-claim path remained explicitly unexercised.
acceptance: two duplicate create-if-absent attempts for the same fingerprint yield exactly one durable repository pin
the losing attempt receives collision/error evidence and does not overwrite winner bytes
winner file bytes remain unchanged after the losing attempt
no queue/current/human accepted/served authority is promoted
title: Repository-host discovery proposal-pin canary
mission: Exercise the canonical GitHub proposal-claim path with duplicate create attempts, preserve the winner, and bound what remains unproven before calling the repository-host race canary complete.

information_gain.reason: Closes the host-specific create-if-absent/no-overwrite uncertainty for sequential duplicate attempts on the real canonical GitHub path.

regression_prevention.reason: Makes it harder to mistake local filesystem atomicity for repository-host race evidence and preserves a precise remaining concurrency boundary.

proven: canonical repository path accepts one create-if-absent winner
later create without update SHA cannot overwrite the winner
winner bytes remain the original candidate pin
candidate path confers no execution or promotion authority
not_yet_proven: true simultaneous/concurrent duplicate create race against the same absent path

falsification.claim_to_test: GitHub repository create-if-absent on the canonical proposal-claim path preserves one winner without silent overwrite under duplicate attempts.
falsification.disconfirming_evidence: A second create succeeds as a create, silently replaces winner bytes, or two truly concurrent creates both establish distinct winner states for one fingerprint.
falsification.test_or_observation: One create succeeded; a second create to the same path without SHA was rejected by the host; winner was fetched afterward and retained original bytes. A separate concurrent canary is still required for simultaneous race semantics.
falsification.pass_condition: Exactly one durable winner and every losing create fails without changing winner bytes.
falsification.fail_condition: Multiple winners or any silent overwrite.
falsification.stop_or_boundary_condition: Do not promote the race canary to full PASS until simultaneous create attempts are exercised or an equivalent host-level atomicity guarantee is independently verified.
